title: Signature Safe-Browsing Compass
body:
The Signature Safe-Browsing Compass is Manon's original design for a small check that runs in the reader's head before any link is followed. The compass has four points: the address, the sender, the request, and the feeling, and a link proceeds only when all four point the same way. Its premise is that a single check can be fooled, but four independent checks rarely fail together, and the compass is deliberately slow, because its slowness is the protection.

The design exists because speed is the trick's ally: every deceptive page benefits when the reader moves faster than thought.

Signature design doctrine. Every Signature design in this pair follows three rules: teach one habit at a time, make the safe action the easy action, and never shame the learner for a mistake, because shame stops people from reporting problems early, when help is still easy.

The working method is Signature address-compass check. Follow these steps in order:

  1. Read the address point: does the domain match the service you know
  2. Read the sender point: did this link arrive through a channel you trust
  3. Read the request point: does the page ask for something it should not need
  4. Read the feeling point: does urgency or flattery push you to hurry
  5. Proceed only when all four points agree, and stop when any one disagrees

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record was executed at build time, so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. The output reads: OK :: Address point agrees; OK :: Sender point agrees; OK :: Request point agrees; OK :: Feeling point calm, not rushed; ok: 4/4; VERDICT: PASS - all checks ok. Readers who run the same code with the same inputs will obtain the same output, which is the reproducibility standard every record here must meet.

Use and limits. The compass is a habit design, not a tool that inspects pages, and it cannot see inside a genuine page that has itself been altered. Its strength is consistency: used on every link, it catches the careless click that a selective check misses. A common mistake is using the compass only on suspicious-looking pages, since the pages that pass a glance are the ones it is for. title: Signature Passphrase Story Method
body:
The Signature Passphrase Story Method builds a passphrase from a tiny invented story whose images only the owner knows. The story might run: a river, a candle, a mountain, a guitar, and the passphrase is those four words in order. Because the story is a picture rather than a rule, it survives in memory without being written down, and because the words are unrelated, guessing them is work multiplied by each added word.

The design treats memory as the real constraint: a secret that cannot be remembered will be written down, and a written secret is a found secret.

Signature design doctrine. Every Signature design in this pair follows three rules: teach one habit at a time, make the safe action the easy action, and never shame the learner for a mistake, because shame stops people from reporting problems early, when help is still easy.

The working method is Signature story-built passphrases. Follow these steps in order:

  1. Invent a short scene with four unrelated objects
  2. Take the object words in scene order as the passphrase
  3. Check that no word is a name, date, or public fact about you
  4. Give each important account its own scene
  5. Store the scenes in a password manager's notes only as hints, never as the words themselves

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record was executed at build time, so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. The output reads: OK len=28 min=20 :: story passphrase; TOO SHORT len=4 min=20 :: short password; OK len=31 min=20 :: long story passphrase; long enough: 2/3; VERDICT: REVIEW - short values need attention. Readers who run the same code with the same inputs will obtain the same output, which is the reproducibility standard every record here must meet.

Use and limits. The method helps memory but does not replace uniqueness: two accounts sharing one story share one fate. It also assumes the service accepts long passphrases, and where a service limits length, the design's fallback is a shorter scene plus a second factor. A common mistake is choosing a scene from real life, such as your street and your school, which an acquaintance could guess. title: Signature Calm-Check Pause
body:
The Signature Calm-Check Pause is Manon's original design for a forced pause between an urgent message and any action on it. The pause is a fixed ritual: set the message aside, drink water, and return after a set number of minutes, during which the claim is checked through a channel the message did not supply. Its premise is that urgency is manufactured precisely to prevent checking, so the pause removes the manufacturer's advantage.

The design exists because willpower fails under pressure, while a ritual performed the same way every time does not need willpower.

Signature design doctrine. Every Signature design in this pair follows three rules: teach one habit at a time, make the safe action the easy action, and never shame the learner for a mistake, because shame stops people from reporting problems early, when help is still easy.

The working method is Signature pause before urgent action. Follow these steps in order:

  1. Notice the urgency and name it aloud: this message wants speed
  2. Set the message aside for a fixed pause and do something unrelated
  3. Check the claim through a channel you already trust
  4. Act only on what the independent check confirms
  5. Report the message if the check contradicts it

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record was executed at build time, so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. The output reads: OK :: Urgency noticed and named; OK :: Fixed pause taken before acting; OK :: Claim checked through a trusted channel; OK :: Action matched only the verified claim; ok: 4/4; VERDICT: PASS - all checks ok. Readers who run the same code with the same inputs will obtain the same output, which is the reproducibility standard every record here must meet.

Use and limits. The pause is a personal ritual, not a guarantee: a genuine emergency can also demand speed, and the design's answer is that genuine emergencies can be verified through a trusted channel too. It does not cover messages that are threats, which should be preserved and reported. A common mistake is pausing only for messages that look like tricks, since the convincing ones are the ones that do not look like tricks. title: Signature Share-Less Ledger
body:
The Signature Share-Less Ledger is Manon's original design for a private note kept before anything is published. Each entry lists what the post shows, who could see it, and what it reveals about routine, location, and relationships. The ledger's rule is that a post is published only when its entry is complete, which forces the review to happen while it can still change the outcome.

The design treats publishing as a decision with a paper trail, because decisions with a trail are made more carefully than impulses.

Signature design doctrine. Every Signature design in this pair follows three rules: teach one habit at a time, make the safe action the easy action, and never shame the learner for a mistake, because shame stops people from reporting problems early, when help is still easy.

The working method is Signature before-sharing ledger. Follow these steps in order:

  1. Write what the post shows, including background details
  2. List who can see it and who might pass it on
  3. Note what it reveals about routine, location, and relationships
  4. Remove one detail before publishing whenever the entry feels long
  5. Keep the ledger private and review it monthly for patterns

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record was executed at build time, so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. The output reads: OK :: Post contents listed before publishing; OK :: Audience and onward sharing noted; OK :: Routine and location revelations noted; OK :: One detail removed where the entry felt long; ok: 4/4; VERDICT: PASS - all checks ok. Readers who run the same code with the same inputs will obtain the same output, which is the reproducibility standard every record here must meet.

Use and limits. The ledger is a personal discipline, not a filter that inspects posts, and it cannot recall copies once a post is published. Its value is in the pause it creates and the patterns a monthly review reveals about what a person habitually reveals. A common mistake is keeping the ledger in the same app as the post, where it becomes one more thing to share by accident. Checks performed on this record: schema completeness, field consistency, teaching ladder placement, and demo re-execution, all passing at build time.

title: Signature Shared-Network Guard
body:
The Signature Shared-Network Guard is Manon's original design for a set of rules that switch on whenever a device joins a network it does not own. The guard's rules are: no sensitive accounts on open networks, encrypted connections only, automatic joining off, and the network forgotten after use. The rules are written as a card kept with the device, so they are followed even when traveling and tired.

The design exists because travel is when judgment is worst and networks are least trustworthy, so the rules must not depend on judgment.

Signature design doctrine. Every Signature design in this pair follows three rules: teach one habit at a time, make the safe action the easy action, and never shame the learner for a mistake, because shame stops people from reporting problems early, when help is still easy.

The working method is Signature open-network guard rules. Follow these steps in order:

  1. Confirm an encrypted connection before any sign-in
  2. Refuse sensitive accounts on any network with no password
  3. Keep automatic joining to open networks switched off
  4. Forget each public network after use
  5. Use a trusted private network service where one is available

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record was executed at build time, so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. The output reads: OK :: Encrypted connection confirmed; OK :: Sensitive accounts refused on open network; OK :: Automatic joining off; OK :: Network forgotten after use; ok: 4/4; VERDICT: PASS - all checks ok. Readers who run the same code with the same inputs will obtain the same output, which is the reproducibility standard every record here must meet.

Use and limits. The guard is a rules card, not a network tool, and it cannot hide which sites are visited from a network operator. Its protection is behavioral: it removes the moments when an unencrypted sign-in happens casually. A common mistake is making exceptions for one quick check, since one quick check is all a session needs to be taken. title: Signature Report-and-Block Card
body:
The Signature Report-and-Block Card is Manon's original design for a wallet-sized procedure: save, block, report, tell. The card's order matters: evidence is saved before blocking, because blocking can hide the evidence; reporting follows, because a report without evidence is a complaint without proof; telling a trusted person comes last, so the story is told once, calmly, with the evidence in hand.

The design treats the order of actions as the innovation, because most failed reports fail on order, not on effort.

Signature design doctrine. Every Signature design in this pair follows three rules: teach one habit at a time, make the safe action the easy action, and never shame the learner for a mistake, because shame stops people from reporting problems early, when help is still easy.

The working method is Signature evidence-first reporting card. Follow these steps in order:

  1. Save the message with sender and date visible
  2. Block the account to stop further contact
  3. Report through the service's own tool with the saved evidence
  4. Tell a trusted person and keep a copy of the evidence
  5. Do not re-engage with the sender while the report is pending

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record was executed at build time, so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. The output reads: OK :: Evidence saved before blocking; OK :: Account blocked; OK :: Report filed with evidence; OK :: Trusted person told; ok: 4/4; VERDICT: PASS - all checks ok. Readers who run the same code with the same inputs will obtain the same output, which is the reproducibility standard every record here must meet.

Use and limits. The card is a procedure, not a promise of removal, and services differ in how they act on reports. Where harm is serious or threatening, the card is a first step, not a substitute for contacting authorities or a support organization. A common mistake is blocking first and then discovering the evidence is gone with the conversation. Checks performed on this record: schema completeness, field consistency, teaching ladder placement, and demo re-execution, all passing at build time.

title: Signature Settings Map
body:
The Signature Settings Map is Manon's original design for a one-page map of an account's settings, drawn by the user on first setup. The map lists each section, what it controls, and the user's chosen value, so later changes can be compared against the map instead of guessed. Its premise is that settings are forgotten because they are scattered, and a map makes the scattered visible.

The design exists because a setting nobody can find again is a setting nobody will ever review.

Signature design doctrine. Every Signature design in this pair follows three rules: teach one habit at a time, make the safe action the easy action, and never shame the learner for a mistake, because shame stops people from reporting problems early, when help is still easy.

The working method is Signature settings walkthrough map. Follow these steps in order:

  1. Open every settings section and note what each one controls
  2. Record your chosen value for each section on the map
  3. Set visibility, contact, data-sharing, and advertising choices deliberately
  4. Remove connected apps and devices you no longer use
  5. Compare the live settings against the map after every major update

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record was executed at build time, so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. The output reads: OK :: Every settings section mapped; OK :: Chosen values recorded; OK :: Connected apps pruned; OK :: Map compared after last update; ok: 4/4; VERDICT: PASS - all checks ok. Readers who run the same code with the same inputs will obtain the same output, which is the reproducibility standard every record here must meet.

Use and limits. The map is a personal record, not a tool that reads settings, and services change their settings layout over time, so the map must be redrawn when a service redesigns. Its value is the comparison habit, not the paper itself. A common mistake is drawing the map once and filing it where it will never be found again. title: Signature Chat-and-Video Code
body:
The Signature Chat-and-Video Code is Manon's original design for a short code agreed before any live conversation about sensitive matters. The code has four lines: who is in the room, what may be shared, what must never be shown on screen, and how anyone may end the call without explanation. Agreeing the code before the call means nobody must improvise manners under pressure during it.

The design treats live conversation as a room with rules posted on the door, because unposted rules are negotiated by the boldest person present.

Signature design doctrine. Every Signature design in this pair follows three rules: teach one habit at a time, make the safe action the easy action, and never shame the learner for a mistake, because shame stops people from reporting problems early, when help is still easy.

The working method is Signature live-conversation code. Follow these steps in order:

  1. Confirm who is in the room before sensitive topics begin
  2. State what may be shared and what must stay private
  3. Agree that screens showing private material are never shared
  4. Agree that anyone may end the call at once, without explanation
  5. Reconfirm the code when a new person joins mid-call

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record was executed at build time, so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. The output reads: OK :: Room membership confirmed; OK :: Sharing limits stated; OK :: Screen-share ban agreed; OK :: Free exit agreed; ok: 4/4; VERDICT: PASS - all checks ok. Readers who run the same code with the same inputs will obtain the same output, which is the reproducibility standard every record here must meet.

Use and limits. The code is an agreement, not a technical control, and it cannot prevent a participant from recording. Its protection is social: it gives every participant a clear, pre-agreed reason to stop a call that breaks the code. A common mistake is assuming a small group is private because it feels friendly, since friendliness is not a access control. title: Signature Download Gate
body:
The Signature Download Gate is Manon's original design for a gate that every file passes before it is opened. The gate asks three questions: did I expect this file, does its type match what I expected, and has it been scanned. A file that fails any question waits, and a file that arrives unasked never passes at all. The gate is deliberately annoying about unasked files, because unasked files are the ones that cause harm.

The design exists because opening is the dangerous step, and a gate at that step is worth more than a warning after it.

Signature design doctrine. Every Signature design in this pair follows three rules: teach one habit at a time, make the safe action the easy action, and never shame the learner for a mistake, because shame stops people from reporting problems early, when help is still easy.

The working method is Signature file-opening gate. Follow these steps in order:

  1. Ask whether this file was expected and from whom
  2. Compare its type with the type that was expected
  3. Wait for a security scan to complete before opening
  4. Refuse extra features a document asks to enable
  5. Delete unasked files without opening them

Use and limits. The gate is a habit, not a scanner, and scanning cannot catch every new or unusual file. Where a file is essential and its safety is doubtful, the gate's rule is to confirm with the sender through a second channel before opening. A common mistake is letting curiosity open an unasked file just to see what it is. title: Signature Recovery Keychain
body:
The Signature Recovery Keychain is Manon's original design for recovery kept as a physical keychain of paper: backup codes, a recovery contact, and a second-factor backup method, stored away from the device they unlock. The keychain's rule is that recovery must work when the device is lost, stolen, or broken, which means recovery can never live only on that device.

The design treats the lost device as the normal case, not the exception, because recovery is only ever needed when something has already gone wrong.

Signature design doctrine. Every Signature design in this pair follows three rules: teach one habit at a time, make the safe action the easy action, and never shame the learner for a mistake, because shame stops people from reporting problems early, when help is still easy.

The working method is Signature recovery readiness keychain. Follow these steps in order:

  1. Confirm recovery contacts are current and reachable
  2. Write backup codes on paper and store them away from the device
  3. Record a backup method for every second factor
  4. Test recovery once on a low-value account
  5. Review the keychain whenever a phone number or email changes

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record was executed at build time, so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. The output reads: OK :: Recovery contacts current; OK :: Backup codes on paper away from device; OK :: Second-factor backup recorded; OK :: Recovery tested on a low-value account; ok: 4/4; VERDICT: PASS - all checks ok. Readers who run the same code with the same inputs will obtain the same output, which is the reproducibility standard every record here must meet.

Use and limits. The keychain is a personal system, not a service, and recovery contacts are themselves a target: anyone controlling them can often take the account. The design therefore guards the keychain as carefully as a password, and it does not cover recovery from identity theft. A common mistake is storing the keychain in a photo on the device it unlocks, which defeats its entire purpose. title: Signature Safety Circle
body:
The Signature Safety Circle is Manon's original design for teaching safety in small circles of people who already trust each other. Each circle meets briefly, learns one habit, practices it together, and leaves with a written reminder. The circle's rule is that nobody is shamed for a past mistake, because a circle that shames will be told nothing, and a circle told nothing can protect nobody.

The design exists because safety advice from a stranger is ignored, while a habit shown by a trusted person is copied.

Signature design doctrine. Every Signature design in this pair follows three rules: teach one habit at a time, make the safe action the easy action, and never shame the learner for a mistake, because shame stops people from reporting problems early, when help is still easy.

The working method is Signature peer-teaching circle. Follow these steps in order:

  1. Gather a small circle of people who trust each other
  2. Teach one habit per meeting, chosen from a member's concern
  3. Practice the habit on each member's own device
  4. Leave a short written reminder in plain words
  5. Meet again and praise the habit, not the fear

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record was executed at build time, so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. The output reads: OK :: Circle gathered from trusted people; OK :: One habit taught per meeting; OK :: Habit practiced on own devices; OK :: Written reminder left; ok: 4/4; VERDICT: PASS - all checks ok. Readers who run the same code with the same inputs will obtain the same output, which is the reproducibility standard every record here must meet.

Use and limits. The circle is a peer method, not professional help, and it does not replace support where harm, threats, or financial loss are involved. Its strength is repetition and trust, not expertise, and circles are encouraged to invite expert guidance for hard cases. A common mistake is turning a circle meeting into a lecture about every danger, which teaches nothing and is not repeated. title: Signature New-Service Scorecard
body:
The Signature New-Service Scorecard is Manon's original design for scoring a new app or service before it is installed. The scorecard rates permissions against the job, data collection against the notice, deletion and export, and independent reports, each on a simple scale. A service that scores low on any line is not installed until the low line is understood, because a single bad line can outweigh three good ones.

The design treats installation as a purchase decision, and a scorecard as the receipt that makes the decision reviewable later.

Signature design doctrine. Every Signature design in this pair follows three rules: teach one habit at a time, make the safe action the easy action, and never shame the learner for a mistake, because shame stops people from reporting problems early, when help is still easy.

The working method is Signature service-evaluation scorecard. Follow these steps in order:

  1. Score each permission against whether the job needs it
  2. Score data collection against what the notice actually says
  3. Score deletion and export: are both offered and usable
  4. Score independent reports of the service's behavior
  5. Refuse installation while any line scores low and unexplained

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record was executed at build time, so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. The output reads: PASS score=4 threshold=4 :: Permissions fit the job; PASS score=3 threshold=3 :: Data collection understood; PASS score=3 threshold=3 :: Deletion and export offered; PASS score=2 threshold=2 :: Independent reports checked; passing: 4/4; VERDICT: PASS - all scores at threshold. Readers who run the same code with the same inputs will obtain the same output, which is the reproducibility standard every record here must meet.

Use and limits. The scorecard is a judgment aid, not an inspection of the service's servers, and a service can change behavior after installation. Its value is that it forces the questions to be asked before installation, when they still cost nothing. A common mistake is averaging the scores into one number, which lets a terrible permission hide behind a pretty interface. title: Signature Compromise First-Aid Kit
body:
The Signature Compromise First-Aid Kit is Manon's original design for a written kit kept ready before any incident. The kit lists, in order: change the password from a clean device starting with email, revoke sessions, turn on a second factor, review recent activity, and warn contacts. The kit's premise is that a crisis is the worst time to invent a procedure, so the procedure is written while calm and followed while stressed.

The design exists because the first hour after discovery decides containment, and a written kit is faster than memory.

Signature design doctrine. Every Signature design in this pair follows three rules: teach one habit at a time, make the safe action the easy action, and never shame the learner for a mistake, because shame stops people from reporting problems early, when help is still easy.

The working method is Signature first-response kit. Follow these steps in order:

  1. Change the password from a trusted device, starting with email
  2. Revoke active sessions and signed-in devices
  3. Turn on a second factor and record its backup
  4. Review recent activity, messages sent, and settings changed
  5. Warn contacts and report the incident

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record was executed at build time, so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. The output reads: OK :: Password changed from a trusted device; OK :: Sessions revoked; OK :: Second factor on; OK :: Activity reviewed; ok: 4/4; VERDICT: PASS - all checks ok. Readers who run the same code with the same inputs will obtain the same output, which is the reproducibility standard every record here must meet.

Use and limits. The kit contains a typical account compromise but does not cover a fully compromised device, which may need professional cleaning or a fresh install, nor financial fraud, which needs the bank's and authorities' processes promptly. It does not promise recovery of lost data or money. A common mistake is improvising the response in the moment and forgetting to revoke sessions, which leaves the intruder inside. title: Signature Household Safety Charter
body:
The Signature Household Safety Charter is Manon's original design for a one-page charter signed, in spirit, by everyone in a household. The charter names who manages the router, who keeps backup codes, the rules for children and guests, and the response steps for a lost device or a suspicious message. Its premise is that shared networks make safety a household matter, not an individual one.

The design treats the household as a single network with many users, so its safety must be agreed, not assumed.

Signature design doctrine. Every Signature design in this pair follows three rules: teach one habit at a time, make the safe action the easy action, and never shame the learner for a mistake, because shame stops people from reporting problems early, when help is still easy.

The working method is Signature household safety charter. Follow these steps in order:

  1. List every device, account, and shared holder in the household
  2. Assign router duties and backup-code keeping by name
  3. Write rules for children, guests, and shared devices plainly
  4. Agree response steps for a lost device and a suspicious message
  5. Review the charter together twice a year and after any move

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record was executed at build time, so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. The output reads: OK :: Devices and accounts listed; OK :: Duties assigned by name; OK :: Rules for children and guests written; OK :: Response steps agreed; ok: 4/4; VERDICT: PASS - all checks ok. Readers who run the same code with the same inputs will obtain the same output, which is the reproducibility standard every record here must meet.

Use and limits. A charter helps a household that can agree, but it cannot force agreement where trust is broken or control is misused. Where a member uses devices or accounts to control or harm another, the charter is not the right tool, and outside help should be sought. A common mistake is signing a charter once and never reviewing it, since households, devices, and children all change. title: Signature Two-Worlds Divider
body:
The Signature Two-Worlds Divider is Manon's original design for a hard line between work and personal digital life. The divider's rules are: separate accounts with separate passwords, separate browser profiles or devices, no forwarding of work material to personal accounts, and a clean handover when changing jobs. Its premise is that blending is convenient until one world falls, and then it drags the other down with it.

The design exists because a single account for everything makes every compromise total.

Signature design doctrine. Every Signature design in this pair follows three rules: teach one habit at a time, make the safe action the easy action, and never shame the learner for a mistake, because shame stops people from reporting problems early, when help is still easy.

The working method is Signature work-personal divider. Follow these steps in order:

  1. Keep work and personal accounts separate, with separate passwords
  2. Use separate browser profiles or devices for the two worlds
  3. Never forward work material to a personal account
  4. Keep personal files off work devices and work files off personal devices
  5. Hand back access cleanly when changing jobs

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record was executed at build time, so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. The output reads: OK :: Separate accounts in use; OK :: Separate profiles or devices in use; OK :: No work forwarding to personal accounts; OK :: Clean handover on job change; ok: 4/4; VERDICT: PASS - all checks ok. Readers who run the same code with the same inputs will obtain the same output, which is the reproducibility standard every record here must meet.

Use and limits. Perfect separation is not always possible, especially where an employer provides only one device, and the design does not override any employer's policy. Its fallback where separation is impossible is separate profiles and strict forwarding rules. A common mistake is keeping one blended account because separation feels like extra work, which it is, and which is the point. title: Signature Evergreen Safety Drill
body:
The Signature Evergreen Safety Drill is Manon's original design for a seasonal drill that keeps safety knowledge from decaying. Each season the drill picks one habit, practices it, teaches it to someone else, and retires one habit that no longer fits the devices in use. Its premise is that safety knowledge decays quietly, and only a drill that is repeated on a schedule notices the decay.

The design treats safety as a garden, not a monument: what is not tended is overgrown by new tricks and new features.

Signature design doctrine. Every Signature design in this pair follows three rules: teach one habit at a time, make the safe action the easy action, and never shame the learner for a mistake, because shame stops people from reporting problems early, when help is still easy.

The working method is Signature seasonal safety drill. Follow these steps in order:

  1. Pick one habit to practice this season
  2. Practice it on your own accounts and devices
  3. Teach it to someone else, which tests your own understanding
  4. Retire one habit that no longer fits your devices
  5. Record the drill so next season starts from a list, not from memory

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record was executed at build time, so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. Its skill is filtering: keeping the habits that fit one's own accounts and dropping the ones that do not. A common mistake is collecting tips without ever practicing one, since unpracticed knowledge fails under pressure.
